Jaroslaw Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Jarosław, Poland

Not demolished. Until the end of the 17th century, Jarosław's Jews were buried in Przemyśl; in 1700, the community obtained permission from the Vaad Arba Aracot (Council of Four Lands), documented at several other sites in this collection, to establish its own cemetery. Jarosław's own synagogue had earlier hosted the Vaad's summer meetings from the second half of the 17th century. After the death in 1849 of the local tzadik Shimon ben Yisrael Maryles, an ohel was built over his grave, in which his successors were also buried; it was rebuilt in 2005. During WWII, tombstones made of precious stone were taken to Germany, and the rest were used for construction; executions and unmarked mass burials also took place at the cemetery.
